summary: # CLO Techniques Teaching Classroom: How to Make a T-Shirt Ribbed Collar ## Introduction Today, I will introduce the T-shirt Loewenling. ## Step 1: Preparing the T-Shirt First, we have the T-shirt on. Place the Loewenling on the right spot. After opening the arrangement point, we put Rowan 0 on a suitable arrangement point. Because it ends on the backside, we arrange it on the other side of the arrangement point. ## Step 2: Adjusting the Arrangement Then, adjust its arrangement position, ensuring the distance between the arrow and the X is correct. After adjusting, we sew. ## Step 3: Sewing Process For sewing, we can use our free sewing 1 to N. First, sew our Rowan 1, then press the Shift key. Next, sew this circle of our circle. Start sewing from this point on the backside. After sewing, we sew the sewing line on both sides of our Rowan. ## Step 4: Simulation and Tool Adjustment After sewing, we can simulate and press the control key. Following this, switch our tool to the adjustment panel. After selecting our panel, right-click to print. Once printed, simulate again. After simulation, turn off the simulation. ## Step 5: Creating a Fold Line Next, we need to create a fold line. Use our tool to select the top and bottom two sides and create this line in the middle. Show our inner line. Then, use the fold arrangement tool to select our inner line. ## Step 6: Folding the Collar Utilize the positioning ball and the tip of the tool to fold. When we fold, we turn around to see if we don't need to turn over. We don't want our grid to be folded. Then, set the fold angle of our fold to zero. After this, sew the top and bottom two lines. The sewing line type is changed to "Turn." This step is very important. ## Step 7: Final Adjustments Then, simulate again. After simulation, adjust the panel tool. Select our panel and untie it. Simulate once more. Then, apply the fabric of the pattern to the panel. Find the fabric of the pattern in the window, select the panel, and apply it. ## Conclusion In this way, we are done. We can improve the quality of this clothing and fill in the color of the pattern. After simulating, we stop the simulation and hide the model. Let's take a look at our pattern circle. Its fold line is a little uneven, so we can use our inner line tool to add 1 mm and give it grid detail to make our fold line more round. This is the production of our T-shirt pattern circle. We will follow the rule that the needle is exposed to hit each bend of the pattern. So there we go: to this volt, to this width, to this divide, and set this value to zero.
